title: Contraception: Method Choice and Medical Eligibility

evidenceAudit.scope: Woman of reproductive age asking for contraception in primary care, an antenatal or postnatal clinic or the emergency department in Saudi Arabia: confirming she is not pregnant, checking medical eligibility with the World Health Organization based checklists, choosing and starting a method (combined pill, progestogen-only pill, implant, hormonal or copper coil, depot injection), advice on missed doses, bleeding changes and follow-up, and emergency contraception. Built on the Saudi Ministry of Health Family Planning National Guidelines 2023 (adapted from the World Health Organization handbook), cross-checked with the 2024 United States eligibility criteria and practice recommendations, with doses, administration and contraindications from product labels.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-20.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: Saudi Ministry of Health Family Planning National Guidelines 2023 are the main source; they are based on the World Health Organization 2015 fifth-edition eligibility criteria, which is older than the 2024 United States criteria. Where the two disagree (for example postpartum timing of combined pills, lamotrigine, treated hypertension) the Saudi text is followed and the United States category is shown in the comparison table.
Printed page numbers (p. N) for the Saudi guideline were read from the page markers in an automated text extraction of the PDF and may be off by one page; check against the PDF.
The Saudi guideline lists SFDA registered products in Annex 8 only as examples; the live SFDA register could not be opened, so current registration was not verified for any product.

Doses, dilution, administration method and contraindications come from the product label named in each regimen row; the desogestrel pill uses the UK summary of product characteristics (the same molecule as the registered Cerazette), the implant and coil use the US labels (the registered products are Implanon NXT and Mirena), and the combined pill uses the US Yasmin label (drospirenone 3 mg and ethinylestradiol 30 microgram; Annex 8 lists Yasmin).

The licensed duration of the implant (3 years in some markets, 5 years on the US label) and of the levonorgestrel coil (8 years on the US label) differ by market; check the local product leaflet for the duration to quote.
Ulipristal acetate (ella) is described in the Saudi guideline but is not listed in Annex 8; its availability in Saudi Arabia was not verified.
The copper intrauterine device (Annex 8 lists Cu 380) is covered in the steps and eligibility checklist but not written as a regimen because no device label was opened.

Combined patch, vaginal ring, monthly injectables, barrier methods, fertility awareness, lactational amenorrhoea method and sterilisation are described in the Saudi guideline but are not written as regimens here.

The Saudi guideline allows a repeat depot injection up to 4 weeks late; the United States practice recommendations allow up to 15 weeks from the last injection; the US label says 13 weeks and a pregnancy check beyond that. The Saudi interval is used.
Normal values for blood pressure and body mass index are standard adult thresholds used in the eligibility checklists.
Differentials follow standard clinical practice and were not drawn from one source section.
Figures were read through automated extraction of the PDF, CDC web text and DailyMed or emc label text; spot-check each dose against the source during clinical review.

SFDA: listed in Annex 8 of the Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023 (drugs registered in the Saudi Food and Drug Authority); the live SFDA register could not be opened from this environment, so current registration was not re-checked.

pathophysiology.summary: Combined pills (estrogen plus progestogen) and progestogen-only pills thicken cervical mucus and stop or reduce ovulation (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 2 Oral Contraceptive Pills, p. 19 and p. 33). Implants, depot injections and the levonorgestrel coil release a progestogen continuously; the implant and injection mainly prevent ovulation, and the coil mainly thickens cervical mucus and thins the endometrium (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 4 and Chapter 6; Mirena label, Section 12). The copper coil works as a spermicidal and anti-implantation device and can also be used as emergency contraception within 5 days of unprotected sex (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 3, p. 52). Emergency contraceptive pills prevent or delay ovulation; they do not work if she is already pregnant (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 3, p. 48). Effectiveness depends on the method: implants and coils work as well as sterilisation without daily effort, while pills and injections depend on being taken or given on time (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 1, Effectiveness table; US SPR 2024, Appendix on effectiveness). Estrogen raises the risk of blood clots, stroke and heart attack in women with certain medical conditions, so methods with estrogen are avoided in them and progestogen-only or non-hormonal methods are used (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 2, p. 20 to p. 23; US MEC 2024, Summary of changes).

symptoms: Request for a reliable method before or after marriage or after birth, to space pregnancies (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 1, Family planning).
Request for emergency contraception after unprotected sex, a condom accident, missed pills or a late injection (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 3, p. 48).
Problems with a current method: irregular bleeding, no bleeding, headache, weight change, mood change (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 2, Managing any problems).
Needs a method that is safe with a medical condition (hypertension, diabetes, migraine, previous clot, epilepsy, HIV) (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 1, Medical eligibility).
physicalSigns: Blood pressure measured at the visit (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 2, p. 21).
Body mass index and smoking status recorded (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 2, p. 20 and p. 21).
For a coil: pelvic examination to find uterine position and exclude cervical or vaginal infection (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5, Pelvic screening and examination).
For a returning implant user: implant palpable under the skin of the upper arm (Nexplanon label, Section 2.2 and Section 5.1).
redFlags: Possible pregnancy that the pregnancy checklist cannot rule out: do not insert a coil or implant or start a depot injection until pregnancy is excluded (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Pregnancy Checklist job aid, p. 239).

Current or past deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, stroke, heart attack or breast cancer: no combined pill; check the method-specific category before any hormonal method (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 2, p. 22; US MEC 2024, Table K1).
Migraine with aura, smoker aged 35 or older, or blood pressure 160/100 mm Hg or higher: no estrogen (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 2, p. 20 to p. 22).

Pregnancy with a coil in place: remove it and assess for ectopic pregnancy; lower abdominal pain or missed period with a coil, implant or progestogen-only method needs urgent assessment for ectopic pregnancy (Mirena label, Section 5.1).
Fever, pelvic pain, foul discharge after coil insertion: possible pelvic infection or sepsis; examine promptly (Mirena label, Section 5.3 and Section 5.4).
Implant not palpable: do not delay; locate by ultrasound and refer (Nexplanon label, Section 2.3 and Section 5.1).
precipitants: Smoking, especially age 35 or older (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 2, p. 20).
Obesity and previous clot raise the risk with estrogen (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 2, p. 20; US MEC 2024, Table K1).
Recent childbirth, caesarean section, transfusion, postpartum haemorrhage or pre-eclampsia: extra clot risk before 6 weeks (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 2, p. 20).
Enzyme-inducing medicines (rifampicin, rifabutin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, topiramate and others) lower the effect of hormonal methods (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 2, p. 23).

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Missed period or unprotected sex without a reliable method; the pregnancy checklist and a urine pregnancy test decide; do not start a long-acting method if pregnancy cannot be excluded (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Pregnancy Checklist job aid, p. 239).

differentials.condition: Ectopic pregnancy in a woman using a progestogen method
differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Lower abdominal pain, missed period or abnormal bleeding while using a coil, implant or injection (Mirena label, Section 5.1; Nexplanon label, Section 5.4).

differentials.condition: Abnormal uterine bleeding unrelated to the method
differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Unexplained bleeding that suggests pregnancy or disease: delay implants, injections and coils until assessed (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 4, p. 60).

differentials.condition: Pelvic infection or sexually transmitted infection
differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Purulent discharge, pelvic pain, cervical tenderness; delay a coil until treated (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5, Medical eligibility; Mirena label, Section 4).

differentials.condition: Polycystic ovary syndrome or thyroid disease causing irregular bleeding
differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Irregular cycles before starting any method; hormonal pills often used for cycle control (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 2, p. 19, benefits).

Irregular bleeding in the first months of an implant, injection, coil or progestogen-only pill, which is common and not harmful (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 2, p. 40; Nexplanon label, Section 5.3).

ruleIn.expectedFinding: All answers no (pregnancy cannot be ruled out by the checklist)
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Use the checklist; if all answers are no, rule out pregnancy by other means (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Pregnancy Checklist job aid, p. 239).
ruleIn.normalValue: At least one yes answer allows reasonable certainty she is not pregnant

clinicalManagement.title: Counsel and respect her choice
actions: Offer all methods, explain effectiveness, side effects, bleeding changes, return of fertility and that only condoms protect against infection (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 1, Counseling).

Ask about her plans, partner views, breastfeeding, and what she can manage (daily pill, injection every 3 months, long-acting method) (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 1, Counseling).
Offer the methods in order of effectiveness: implant and coil first, then injection, then pill (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 1, Effectiveness table).

clinicalManagement.title: Confirm she is not pregnant
actions: Use the six-question pregnancy checklist; any yes means you can be reasonably sure she is not pregnant (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Pregnancy Checklist job aid, p. 239).
If all answers are no, use a urine pregnancy test or delay the start with a backup method (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Pregnancy Checklist job aid, p. 239).
Pregnancy cannot be excluded by a test within 3 weeks of unprotected sex: give a barrier method and repeat the test after 3 weeks if no bleeding (US SPR 2024, Section on emergency contraception).

clinicalManagement.title: Check medical eligibility
actions: Ask the method-specific eligibility questions; examinations and tests are not needed for pills, injections or implants (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 2, p. 20).
Measure blood pressure before a combined pill (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 2, p. 21).

For any condition you are unsure of, use the full category tables in Annex 4 and the United States criteria; do not give a category 3 or 4 method where clinical judgment is limited (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 1, Using clinical judgment).
For a coil, take a sexually transmitted infection risk history and examine the pelvis (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5, Pelvic screening).

clinicalManagement.title: Choose and start the method
actions: No estrogen condition and wants a pill: progestogen-only pill (desogestrel 75 microgram) (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 2, p. 34).
No estrogen condition and wants a long-acting method: implant, hormonal coil or depot injection (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 4 to Chapter 6).
Estrogen allowed and wants a pill: combined pill (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 2, p. 21).

Start on days 1 to 5 of the period (pills, implant) or up to day 7 (injection, hormonal coil) with no backup; at any other time when pregnancy is excluded, with backup for 7 days (2 days for a progestogen-only pill) (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 2, p. 24 and p. 36; Chapter 4, p. 60).

Postpartum: coils within 48 hours or after 4 weeks; progestogen-only methods at any time; combined pill from 6 weeks if breastfeeding partially or 3 weeks if not breastfeeding and no clot risk (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 2, p. 24 to p. 25; Chapter 5, p. 97).

clinicalManagement.title: Offer emergency contraception when needed
clinicalManagement.timeframe: As soon as possible, up to 5 days
actions: Offer levonorgestrel 1.5 mg or ulipristal 30 mg as soon as possible within 5 days; ulipristal is more effective at 3 to 5 days (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 3, p. 46; US SPR 2024, Section on emergency contraception).
Offer a copper coil within 5 days as the most effective emergency method, and it can stay as ongoing contraception (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 3, p. 52).

Start a regular method straight away after levonorgestrel; wait 5 to 6 days after ulipristal and use a barrier method until then (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 3, p. 50 to p. 51; ella label, Section 2.2).

clinicalManagement.title: Teach use, missed doses and follow-up
clinicalManagement.timeframe: Before she leaves; review per method
actions: Give up to 3 months of pills at the start; show the pack; explain backup methods (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 2, p. 26).

Combined pill: take a missed pill as soon as possible; 3 or more missed pills in a row need backup for 7 days and may need emergency contraception (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 2, p. 28).
Progestogen-only pill: a pill more than 3 hours late (12 hours for the desogestrel pill) needs backup for 2 days (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 2, p. 39).
Injection: return every 3 months; the next dose can be given up to 2 weeks early or 4 weeks late (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 4, Comparing injectables).
Coil: review 4 to 6 weeks after insertion and yearly; implant: check the site and bleeding; all users: blood pressure check yearly (Mirena label, Section 2.3; Yasmin label, Section 5.13).
Bring her back for any severe pain, heavy bleeding, missed period, headache with visual loss, leg swelling or chest pain (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 2, Warning signs).

regimens.indication: Prevention of pregnancy in women who can use estrogen
regimens.patientGroup: Women of reproductive age with no estrogen contraindication
regimens.dose: One yellow active tablet (drospirenone 3 mg plus ethinylestradiol 0.03 mg) daily for 21 days, then one white inactive tablet daily for days 22 to 28; start the next 28-day pack the day after the last white tablet. Dilution and preparation: none; oral dose form, no reconstitution.
regimens.route: Oral, one tablet at the same time every day with liquid, with or without food (Yasmin label, Section 2.1 and Section 2.2)
regimens.duration: As long as contraception is wanted and she stays eligible; review yearly
adjustments: Start on day 1 of the period (no backup) or any day after pregnancy is excluded with a non-hormonal backup for 7 days (Yasmin label, Section 2.2).

Postpartum, not breastfeeding: start no earlier than 4 weeks (Yasmin label, Section 2.2); the Saudi guideline allows days 21 to 28 if she has no extra clot risk and 6 weeks if she has one (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 2, p. 24 to p. 25).

Breastfeeding: fully or nearly fully breastfeeding wait until 6 months or until milk is not the main food; partially breastfeeding from 6 weeks (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 2, p. 20).
Renal impairment, hepatic impairment and adrenal insufficiency are contraindicated because drospirenone can cause hyperkalaemia (Yasmin label, Section 4 and Section 5.2).

Missed pills: one pill, take it as soon as possible; two in a row in week 1 or 2, take two now and two tomorrow with backup for 7 days; three or more or two in week 3 or 4, discard the rest and start a new pack with backup for 7 days (Yasmin label, Section 2.3).
Vomiting or severe diarrhoea can reduce absorption: treat as missed pills (Yasmin label, Section 2.4).

SFDA: listed in Annex 8 of the Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023 (drugs registered in the Saudi Food and Drug Authority); the live SFDA register could not be opened from this environment, so current registration was not re-checked.
monitoring: Blood pressure at least yearly (Yasmin label, Section 5.13).
Serum potassium in the first cycle if she takes ACE inhibitors, angiotensin receptor blockers, potassium-sparing diuretics, NSAIDs daily or heparin (Yasmin label, Section 5.2).
Warning signs of a clot or stroke: leg pain or swelling, chest pain, breathlessness, severe headache, visual loss (Yasmin label, Boxed Warning and Section 5.1).
contraindications: Smoker aged over 35 (boxed warning, Yasmin label, Section 4).

Current or past deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism; cerebrovascular disease; coronary artery disease; thrombogenic valve or rhythm disease; inherited or acquired clotting disorder (Yasmin label, Section 4).
Uncontrolled hypertension; diabetes with vascular disease; migraine with focal neurological symptoms, or migraine with or without aura over age 35 (Yasmin label, Section 4).
Breast cancer now or in the past; liver tumour or liver disease; renal impairment; adrenal insufficiency; undiagnosed abnormal uterine bleeding (Yasmin label, Section 4).
Hepatitis C medicines containing ombitasvir, paritaprevir and ritonavir, with or without dasabuvir (Yasmin label, Section 4).

regimens.indication: Prevention of pregnancy, including while breastfeeding
regimens.patientGroup: Women who cannot or prefer not to use estrogen
regimens.dose: One 75 microgram tablet daily at about the same time, with a 24-hour interval between tablets, with no break between packs. Dilution and preparation: none; oral dose form, no reconstitution.
regimens.route: Oral, one tablet each day continuously; first tablet on day 1 of bleeding (Cerazette SmPC, Section 4.2)
regimens.frequency: Once daily without a pill-free week
regimens.duration: As long as contraception is wanted; review yearly
adjustments: Starting days 2 to 5 of the cycle: add a barrier method for the first 7 days; after a first-trimester abortion start immediately (Cerazette SmPC, Section 4.2).

After birth or a second-trimester abortion start between day 21 and day 28; later starts need a barrier method for 7 days (Cerazette SmPC, Section 4.2); the Saudi guideline allows breastfeeding women to start any time up to 6 months with no backup (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 2, p. 35).

Late tablet: less than 12 hours late, take it and continue; more than 12 hours late, take it and use backup for 7 days (Cerazette SmPC, Section 4.2); the Saudi guideline says abstain or use backup for 2 days (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 2, p. 39).
Vomiting within 3 to 4 hours, or severe diarrhoea: treat as a missed tablet (Cerazette SmPC, Section 4.2).
Hepatic impairment: not indicated while liver tests are abnormal (Cerazette SmPC, Section 4.2). Renal impairment: no studies (Cerazette SmPC, Section 4.2).
Enzyme inducers: barrier method for the whole time and 28 days after stopping, or choose another method (Cerazette SmPC, Section 4.5).
Lactation: may be used during breastfeeding; watch the infant's growth (Cerazette SmPC, Section 4.6).

SFDA: listed in Annex 8 of the Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023 (drugs registered in the Saudi Food and Drug Authority); the live SFDA register could not be opened from this environment, so current registration was not re-checked.
monitoring: Bleeding pattern; irregular bleeding is common and not harmful; investigate if persistent (Cerazette SmPC, Section 4.2; Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 2, p. 40).
Amenorrhoea: pregnancy test if tablets were missed (Cerazette SmPC, Section 4.2).
Lower abdominal pain or missed period: exclude ectopic pregnancy (Cerazette SmPC, Section 4.4).
contraindications: Active venous thromboembolic disorder (Cerazette SmPC, Section 4.3).
Presence or history of severe liver disease until liver tests normalise (Cerazette SmPC, Section 4.3).
Known or suspected sex-steroid sensitive cancer, such as breast cancer (Cerazette SmPC, Section 4.3).
Undiagnosed vaginal bleeding; hypersensitivity to the active substance or excipients (Cerazette SmPC, Section 4.3).

regimens.indication: Prevention of pregnancy for up to 5 years with one implant
regimens.patientGroup: Women wanting the most effective method, including breastfeeding women and women who cannot use estrogen
regimens.dose: One 68 mg etonogestrel rod, 4 cm long, supplied sterile in a preloaded applicator. Dilution and preparation: none; check the rod is visible in the needle tip before insertion.
regimens.route: Subdermal insertion with the preloaded applicator into the inner side of the non-dominant upper arm over the triceps, 8 to 10 cm above the medial epicondyle and 3 to 5 cm behind the groove between biceps and triceps, by a trained and certified healthcare provider; confirm by palpation straight away (Nexplanon label, Section 2 and Section 2.2)
regimens.duration: Remove by the end of the labelled duration (up to 5 years on the US label); replace at removal if still wanted (Nexplanon label, Section 1 and Section 2.4)
adjustments: Insert on days 1 to 5 of the cycle with no backup; at other times add a barrier method for 7 days and exclude pregnancy (Nexplanon label, Section 2.1).

Switching from a combined pill, ring or patch: insert on the day after the last active tablet; from a progestogen-only pill, insert within 24 hours of the last tablet; from an injection, insert on the day the next injection is due (Nexplanon label, Section 2.1).
Postpartum and breastfeeding: can be inserted any time up to 6 months with no backup if bleeding has not returned (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 6, p. 105).
Insertion and removal need training; deep insertion can cause nerve or vessel injury and make removal difficult (Nexplanon label, Section 5.1 and Section 5.2).
Drug interactions: enzyme-inducing medicines may reduce effect; use a barrier method (Nexplanon label, Section 7; Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 2, p. 23).

SFDA: listed in Annex 8 of the Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023 (drugs registered in the Saudi Food and Drug Authority); the live SFDA register could not be opened from this environment, so current registration was not re-checked.
monitoring: Palpate the implant at every review; if it cannot be felt, locate by ultrasound before removal (Nexplanon label, Section 2.3 and Section 5.1).
Bleeding pattern changes are the commonest reason for removal (Nexplanon label, Section 5.3).
Ectopic pregnancy, ovarian cysts, blood pressure and mood (Nexplanon label, Section 5.4, Section 5.6, Section 5.10 and Section 5.13).
contraindications: Known or suspected pregnancy (Nexplanon label, Section 4).
Current or past thrombosis or thromboembolic disorder (Nexplanon label, Section 4).
Liver tumour (benign or malignant) or active liver disease (Nexplanon label, Section 4).
Undiagnosed abnormal uterine bleeding (Nexplanon label, Section 4).
Known or suspected breast cancer or other progestin-sensitive cancer, now or in the past; allergy to any component (Nexplanon label, Section 4).
regimens.branch: Long-acting method: implant, hormonal coil or injection
regimens.useWhen: Preferred first choice: most effective, no daily action, safe with breastfeeding and when estrogen is not allowed.
regimens.sourceEdition: Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 6 Implants, p. 103 to p. 106; Nexplanon US label, Section 1, Section 2.1 to Section 2.4, Section 4 and Section 5

regimens.indication: Prevention of pregnancy for up to 8 years with one hormonal coil (also treats heavy menstrual bleeding)
regimens.patientGroup: Women wanting a long-acting method, especially with heavy periods
regimens.dose: One levonorgestrel 52 mg intrauterine system releasing about 21 microgram per day at first, falling to about 11 microgram per day at 5 years and 7 microgram per day at 8 years. Dilution and preparation: none; supplied sterile in an inserter, open only at insertion.
regimens.route: Intrauterine insertion by a trained provider using strict aseptic technique and the single-handed inserter; offer analgesia before insertion (Mirena label, Section 2.2)
regimens.duration: Up to 8 years for contraception (up to 5 years for heavy menstrual bleeding); remove and replace at the end of that period (Mirena label, Section 1 and Section 2.1)
adjustments: Insert in the first 7 days of the cycle with no backup, or at any time pregnancy is excluded with a barrier method or abstinence for 7 days (Mirena label, Section 2.2; Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5, p. 97).
Immediately after a first-trimester abortion or miscarriage (not septic) (Mirena label, Section 2.2).

After childbirth: within 48 hours with a trained provider, or wait at least 4 weeks (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5, p. 97); the US label says wait at least 6 weeks or until the uterus is involuted, and warns of higher perforation risk within 6 weeks and in breastfeeding women (Mirena label, Section 2.2 and Section 5.5).
Switching from a pill, patch or ring: insert any time; keep the old method for 7 days or until the end of the cycle (Mirena label, Section 2.2).
Switching from an injection: insert when the next injection is due, or add backup for 7 days if more than 13 weeks since the last injection (Mirena label, Section 2.2).
If pregnancy occurs with the system in place, remove it and evaluate for ectopic pregnancy (Mirena label, Section 5.1 and Section 5.2).

SFDA: listed in Annex 8 of the Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023 (drugs registered in the Saudi Food and Drug Authority); the live SFDA register could not be opened from this environment, so current registration was not re-checked.
monitoring: Review 4 to 6 weeks after insertion and yearly (Mirena label, Section 2.3).
Pelvic pain, fever or foul discharge after insertion: examine for pelvic infection or sepsis (Mirena label, Section 5.3 and Section 5.4).
Missing threads: ultrasound to exclude expulsion or perforation (Mirena label, Section 5.5 and Section 5.6).
contraindications: Pregnancy or suspected pregnancy; not for emergency contraception (Mirena label, Section 4).
Uterine anomaly or fibroids that distort the cavity (Mirena label, Section 4).

Acute pelvic inflammatory disease or past pelvic inflammatory disease without a later intrauterine pregnancy; postpartum endometritis or infected abortion in the past 3 months; untreated acute cervicitis or vaginitis (Mirena label, Section 4).
Known or suspected uterine or cervical cancer; breast cancer or other progestin-sensitive cancer; uterine bleeding of unknown cause (Mirena label, Section 4).
Acute liver disease or liver tumour; a previously inserted coil not removed; hypersensitivity (Mirena label, Section 4).
regimens.branch: Long-acting method: implant, hormonal coil or injection
regimens.useWhen: Choose when she wants a coil, has heavy menstrual bleeding or wants to avoid a systemic implant, and has no pelvic infection, uterine distortion or breast cancer.
regimens.sourceTitle: MIRENA (levonorgestrel intrauterine system): US prescribing information (DailyMed)
regimens.sourceEdition: Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Levonorgestrel Intrauterine Device, p. 95 to p. 99; Mirena US label, Section 1, Section 2.1 to Section 2.3, Section 4 and Section 5

regimens.indication: Prevention of pregnancy by a three-monthly injection
regimens.patientGroup: Women who prefer an injection and cannot or do not want a daily pill or a device
regimens.dose: 150 mg (1 mL) every 3 months (13 weeks). Dilution and preparation: none; shake the vial or prefilled syringe vigorously immediately before use so the dose is a uniform suspension.
regimens.route: Deep intramuscular injection into the gluteal or deltoid muscle with strict aseptic technique; rotate sites; use a longer needle if needed for gluteal injection (Depo-Provera label, Section 2.1)
regimens.duration: Use beyond 2 years is not recommended unless other methods are inadequate because of bone density loss (Depo-Provera label, Section 1 and Section 5.1)
adjustments: First injection in the first 5 days of a normal period or in the first 5 days postpartum; in exclusively breastfeeding mothers give from the sixth postpartum week (Depo-Provera label, Section 2.1); the Saudi guideline allows the injection up to day 7 of the period and from 6 weeks if breastfeeding (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 4, p. 60 to p. 61).

Repeat dose: the Saudi guideline allows 2 weeks early to 4 weeks late (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 4, Comparing injectables); if more than 13 weeks the label says confirm she is not pregnant before the next dose (Depo-Provera label, Section 2.1).
Switching from a combined pill: first injection the day after the last active tablet (Depo-Provera label, Section 2.2).
No dose change for body weight (Depo-Provera label, Section 2.1).
Not suitable with blood pressure 160/100 mm Hg or higher, diabetes with complications, past stroke or heart attack (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 4, p. 59 to p. 61).
Consider bone density in long-term users and in women with risk factors for osteoporosis (Depo-Provera label, Section 5.1).

SFDA: listed in Annex 8 of the Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023 (drugs registered in the Saudi Food and Drug Authority); the live SFDA register could not be opened from this environment, so current registration was not re-checked.
monitoring: Bone health: review the need to continue at 2 years (Depo-Provera label, Section 5.1).
Bleeding changes, weight gain and mood (Depo-Provera label, Section 5.10 to Section 5.12).
Blood pressure and other indicated care at a yearly visit (Depo-Provera label, Section 5.17).
Return of fertility can take about 4 months or more after the last injection (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 4, p. 57).
contraindications: Active thrombophlebitis, current or past thromboembolic disorder or cerebrovascular disease (Depo-Provera label, Section 4).
Known or suspected breast cancer (Depo-Provera label, Section 4).
Significant liver disease (Depo-Provera label, Section 4).
Undiagnosed vaginal bleeding; known hypersensitivity (Depo-Provera label, Section 4).
regimens.branch: Long-acting method: implant, hormonal coil or injection
regimens.useWhen: Choose when she prefers an injection, has no day-to-day pill-taking ability and has no risk factors for bone loss or stroke; not for use longer than 2 years unless other options are inadequate.
regimens.sourceTitle: Depo-Provera CI (medroxyprogesterone acetate injectable suspension 150 mg/mL): US prescribing information (DailyMed)
regimens.sourceEdition: Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 4 Progestin-Only Injectables, p. 57 to p. 63; Depo-Provera CI US label, Section 1, Section 2.1 to Section 2.2, Section 4 and Section 5.1

regimens.indication: Emergency contraception after unprotected sex or contraceptive failure
regimens.patientGroup: All women who are not pregnant, within 5 days
regimens.dose: One 1.5 mg tablet as a single dose, as soon as possible (the Saudi guideline also lists 0.75 mg twice 12 hours apart). Dilution and preparation: none; oral dose form, no reconstitution.
regimens.route: Oral, swallowed whole with water, with or without food (Plan B label, Directions)
regimens.duration: Single use; not for regular contraception
adjustments: Take as soon as possible; the label states within 72 hours (Plan B label, Directions), while the Saudi guideline and the United States recommendations allow use up to 5 days with reduced effect with delay (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 3, p. 46; US SPR 2024, Section on emergency contraception).
Vomiting within 2 hours: repeat the dose (Plan B label, Directions; Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 3, p. 50).
Enzyme inducers (efavirenz, rifampin, anti-seizure medicines) may reduce effect; ask a doctor or pharmacist (Plan B label, Warnings); consider a copper coil instead.
Start or restart ongoing contraception straight away; add a barrier method for 7 days (2 days for a progestogen-only pill) (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 3, p. 50).
No renal or hepatic dose change in the label; no medical condition makes emergency pills unsafe (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 3, p. 48).

SFDA: listed in Annex 8 of the Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023 (drugs registered in the Saudi Food and Drug Authority); the live SFDA register could not be opened from this environment, so current registration was not re-checked.
monitoring: Next period: if more than 7 days late, do a pregnancy test (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 3, p. 50).
Nausea, vomiting, headache and abdominal pain are common and short-lived (Plan B label, Warnings).
Lower abdominal pain after use: consider ectopic pregnancy (US SPR 2024, Section on emergency contraception).
contraindications: Known pregnancy (the pill will not work) (Plan B label, Do not use).
Allergic reaction to levonorgestrel (Plan B label, Allergy alert).
Not for regular birth control (Plan B label, Do not use).
regimens.useWhen: Preferred when she presents within 3 days and ulipristal is not available; registered in Saudi Arabia under several trade names.
regimens.sourceTitle: Plan B One-Step (levonorgestrel 1.5 mg): US drug facts label (DailyMed)
regimens.sourceEdition: Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 3 Emergency Contraceptive Pills, p. 46 to p. 52; Plan B One-Step US label, Directions and Warnings

regimens.indication: Emergency contraception, more effective than levonorgestrel at 3 to 5 days
regimens.patientGroup: Women presenting 3 to 5 days after unprotected sex
regimens.dose: One 30 mg tablet as a single dose as soon as possible within 120 hours (5 days). Dilution and preparation: none; oral dose form, no reconstitution.
regimens.route: Oral, with or without food, at any time in the menstrual cycle (ella label, Section 2.1)
regimens.duration: Single use; do not repeat within the same menstrual cycle (ella label, Section 5.3)
adjustments: Vomiting within 3 hours: consider repeating the dose (ella label, Section 2.3).
Do not use with CYP3A4 inducers such as barbiturates, carbamazepine, oxcarbazepine, phenytoin, rifampin, bosentan, felbamate and griseofulvin (ella label, Section 5.4 and Section 7.1).

Wait at least 5 days before starting or resuming hormonal contraception and use a reliable barrier method until the next period (ella label, Section 2.2); the Saudi guideline says start on day 6 (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 3, p. 50 to p. 51).
No renal or hepatic dose change is given in the label.

SFDA: this exact product is not listed in Annex 8 of the Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023 and the live SFDA register could not be opened, so registration in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check before prescribing.
monitoring: Pregnancy test if the period is more than 7 days late (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 3, p. 50).
Ectopic pregnancy if lower abdominal pain after use; a history of ectopic pregnancy is not a contraindication (ella label, Section 5.2).
Fertility returns quickly; start a regular method (ella label, Section 5.5).
contraindications: Known or suspected pregnancy (ella label, Section 4).
regimens.useWhen: Choose when she presents 3 to 5 days after unprotected sex and the drug is available; avoid with CYP3A4 inducers and do not start hormonal contraception for 5 days.
regimens.sourceTitle: ella (ulipristal acetate) tablet: US prescribing information (DailyMed)
regimens.sourceEdition: Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 3, p. 46 to p. 51; ella US label, Section 1, Section 2.1 to Section 2.3, Section 4 and Section 5

branches.label: Daily pill with estrogen (combined pill)
branches.entryCriteria: Woman who wants a daily pill, is not pregnant, has no condition that excludes estrogen (age under 35 or non-smoker, normal blood pressure, no migraine with aura, no clot or heart disease, no liver tumour, not breastfeeding a baby under 6 months, no enzyme-inducing medicine) and has had the eligibility questions asked.

branches.label: Daily pill without estrogen (progestogen-only pill)
branches.entryCriteria: Woman who wants a daily pill but cannot use estrogen (breastfeeding, smoker aged 35 or older, migraine with aura, high blood pressure, previous clot, diabetes with complications) and has no liver tumour, breast cancer or enzyme-inducing medicine.

branches.label: Long-acting method: implant, hormonal coil or injection
branches.entryCriteria: Woman who wants a method that does not depend on daily action, is not pregnant (checklist or test), has no undiagnosed vaginal bleeding, no breast cancer, no active liver disease or liver tumour and no current deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism off treatment.

branches.label: Emergency contraception after unprotected sex
branches.entryCriteria: Woman with unprotected sex, a contraceptive failure or sexual assault within the last 5 days who is not already pregnant (all women are eligible; there is no medical condition that makes emergency pills unsafe).

medicationPlan.note: Choice of method and eligibility follow the Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023; doses, dilution and preparation, administration and contraindications come from the product label named in each row. All doses are for adults. Where several methods suit the same woman the rows are marked as choose-one. SFDA: listed in Annex 8 of the Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023 (drugs registered in the Saudi Food and Drug Authority); the live SFDA register could not be opened from this environment, so current registration was not re-checked.

diagnosticCriteria.criterion: Category 1 (US MEC and World Health Organization)
diagnosticCriteria.threshold: No restriction: use the method (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 1, Categories table; US MEC 2024, Introduction).
Advantages generally outweigh the risks: can use with careful follow-up (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 1, Categories table; US MEC 2024, Introduction).

Risks usually outweigh the advantages: not usually recommended unless other methods are unavailable or unacceptable, and only with careful clinical judgment and follow-up (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 1, Categories table).
Unacceptable health risk: do not use the method (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 1, Categories table).

diagnosticCriteria.criterion: Reasonably certain she is not pregnant
diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Any one yes to: last period began within 7 days (12 days for a copper coil); abstained since the last period or birth; using a reliable method correctly; gave birth within 4 weeks; fully or nearly fully breastfeeding, no period and baby under 6 months; miscarriage or abortion within 7 days (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Pregnancy Checklist job aid, p. 239; US SPR 2024, Section on how to be reasonably certain).

Age 35 or older and smokes; blood pressure 160/100 or higher (or 140/90 or higher on repeat); migraine with aura; stroke, heart attack or current blood clot; breast cancer; cirrhosis or liver tumour; diabetes for more than 20 years or with organ damage; several risk factors for heart disease (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 2, p. 20 to p. 23).

Fully or nearly fully breastfeeding: start 6 months after birth or when milk is no longer the main food; partially breastfeeding: from 6 weeks (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 2, p. 20).

Up to 15 weeks from the last injection without backup (US SPR 2024)

teaching.scope: Woman of reproductive age asking for contraception in primary care, an antenatal or postnatal clinic or the emergency department in Saudi Arabia: confirming she is not pregnant, checking medical eligibility with the World Health Organization based checklists, choosing and starting a method (combined pill, progestogen-only pill, implant, hormonal or copper coil, depot injection), advice on missed doses, bleeding changes and follow-up, and emergency contraception. Built on the Saudi Ministry of Health Family Planning National Guidelines 2023 (adapted from the World Health Organization handbook), cross-checked with the 2024 United States eligibility criteria and practice recommendations, with doses, administration and contraindications from product labels.
learningObjectives: Ask the eligibility questions and exclude pregnancy before every method.
Offer implants and coils first because they are most effective, then injection, then pills.
Avoid estrogen in smokers aged 35 or older, high blood pressure, migraine with aura, past clot or stroke.
Emergency contraception works best when taken early; a copper coil is the most effective emergency method.
pitfalls: Giving a combined pill to a smoker aged 35 or older.
Starting a combined pill in the first 3 weeks after birth.
Inserting a coil without asking about infection risk.
Giving a repeat depot injection after the window without checking pregnancy.
Missing an ectopic pregnancy in a woman with a coil or implant.
keyPoints: Estrogen is not given if blood pressure is 160/100 or higher, or 140/90 or higher on repeat.
Check pregnancy before inserting a coil or implant or giving the first injection.
Enzyme-inducing medicines reduce the effect of pills, implants and ulipristal.
Do not start hormonal contraception for 5 days after ulipristal.
No method except condoms protects against infection.

patientEducation: Choose the method you will use easily; you can change it at any time.
Take your pill at the same time every day; if you miss pills, follow the pack instructions and use condoms.
Irregular bleeding in the first months of an implant, injection or coil is common and not harmful.
Come back at once for severe pain in the lower abdomen, a missed period, a swollen painful leg, chest pain or a severe headache.
Emergency pills work best the sooner you take them; you can use them up to 5 days after unprotected sex.
Condoms are the only method that also protect against infection.
lifestyleAndDiet: Do not smoke, especially if you use a combined pill.
Keep a healthy weight and blood pressure.
Tell any doctor or pharmacist which contraceptive you use before starting new medicines.
Keep a record of the date for the next injection or for coil or implant removal.
mdtReferrals: Primary care physician or family physician; nurse or midwife trained in contraception; obstetrician and gynaecologist for complex eligibility and removals; pharmacist for interactions; counsellor or psychologist if needed; infectious diseases physician for HIV.
dischargeCriteria: Pregnancy excluded and eligibility checked; method chosen and started with correct backup advice; instructions and warning signs explained; supply or appointment for the next dose, injection or review given; emergency contraception advice and condoms offered.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Implant: check the site and bleeding at 1 to 3 months and yearly; coil: review at 4 to 6 weeks and yearly; pills: review at 3 months and yearly with blood pressure; injection: every 3 months (up to 2 weeks early or 4 weeks late); reassess eligibility at each visit if health or medicines change; remove and replace implants and coils at the end of their licensed duration.
